memory_update.text: VECO should be tracked as an underfollowed equipment candidate in the AI optical-interconnect stack because it has announced $250M+ of InP laser manufacturing equipment orders tied to 800G/1.6T and hyperscale data-center optics.
AXTI should be tracked as a small-cap InP substrate candidate, but it needs current verification on InP capacity expansion, backlog, customer qualification, and China/export-control risk.

ALMU belongs in the speculative_shadow lane as a potential III-V-on-silicon bypass of native InP constraints; keep it out of higher-confidence layers until commercial revenue, yield, and customer qualification are verified.

For compound_photonics_cpo_stack, the underappreciated choke points appear to be InP substrate/device capacity, InP laser manufacturing equipment, MOCVD/ion-beam/wet-processing tools, and manufacturable III-V-on-silicon alternatives rather than only transceiver brands.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed optical test, inspection, precision bonding, and CPO assembly/yield tools; this pass found stronger immediate evidence for InP substrates and InP laser manufacturing equipment.

node: Compound semiconductor photonics, InP substrates, CPO, lasers, photodetectors, epitaxy, etch and bonding equipment
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the compound-photonics/CPO stack finds a two-lane universe: Lumentum as a higher-attention reference anchor for InP lasers, CPO-ready components, and AI data-center optics; and a discovery lane centered on Veeco, AXT, and Aeluma. The most actionable underfollowed mapping is upstream: Veeco for MOCVD/ion-beam/wet-processing tools used in InP laser manufacturing; AXT for InP substrates used in high-speed optical transmission; and Aeluma as a speculative III-V-on-silicon photonics platform that could bypass some native InP substrate constraints if commercial qualification materializes. No buy/sell view is implied.
